bull.b: The move into commercial operations creates a potential recurring revenue base beyond financing. Early physician, patient and payer feedback supports adoption prospects, although the launch remains at an early stage and will require sustained execution.

A substantial liquidity position gives Viridian resources to fund commercialization and clinical development while reducing near-term dependence on capital markets. This strengthens operating flexibility during the transition toward potential profitability.

Securing a qualified commercial manufacturing partner ahead of approval can reduce execution risk and support scalable supply. The ability to use alternate manufacturers also provides flexibility if capacity, regulatory or operational conditions change.

bear.b: Viridian remains substantially unprofitable despite higher revenue, as operating expenses continue to outweigh gross profit. Persistent losses could delay self-sustaining operations and require continued cost control, funding or successful product scaling.

Deeply negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is not yet funding itself. Continued investment in launch activities and pipeline programs may consume liquidity materially before commercial revenues can support ongoing expenditure.

Future growth depends on successful commercialization of Lumvoa and regulatory approval of pipeline programs. Delays, unsuccessful development or weaker adoption would extend losses and reduce the likelihood that projected revenues fund the business through profitability.
